hints: Resolve the three given forces into horizontal components ($x$-direction) and vertical components ($y$-direction).
For equilibrium, the additional balancing force must have components $-X$ and $-Y$, so its magnitude is $\sqrt{X^2 + Y^2}$.
Calculate the angle $\alpha = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{Y}{X}\right)$ and specify the direction clearly relative to the negative $x$-axis.
walkthrough:
Resolve the three given forces along horizontal and vertical axes:
$$X = 18 + 12\sin 60^\circ - 8\sin 30^\circ = 18 + 12\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) - 8(0.5) = 14 + 6\sqrt{3} \approx 24.3923\text{ N}$$
$$Y = 8\cos 30^\circ + 12\cos 60^\circ = 8\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) + 12(0.5) = 6 + 4\sqrt{3} \approx 12.9282\text{ N}$$
For equilibrium, the additional force must have components equal and opposite to $(X, Y)$, so its components are $F_x = -24.3923\text{ N}$ and $F_y = -12.9282\text{ N}$.

Calculate the magnitude of the balancing force using Pythagoras' theorem:
$$F = \sqrt{X^2 + Y^2} = \sqrt{(14 + 6\sqrt{3})^2 + (6 + 4\sqrt{3})^2}$$
$$F = \sqrt{24.3923^2 + 12.9282^2} = \sqrt{594.985 + 167.138} = \sqrt{762.123} \approx 27.6\text{ N}$$

Find the direction of the balancing force:
$$\tan\alpha = \frac{Y}{X} = \frac{6 + 4\sqrt{3}}{14 + 6\sqrt{3}} \approx \frac{12.9282}{24.3923} \approx 0.5300$$
$$\alpha = \tan^{-1}(0.5300) \approx 27.9^\circ$$
Since both components are negative, the force is directed $27.9^\circ$ below the negative $x$-axis.
teacher_walkthrough:
State the condition for equilibrium when a fourth force $\mathbf{F}_4$ is added to three coplanar forces:
$$\Sigma F_x = 0 \implies F_{4x} + X = 0 \implies F_{4x} = -X$$
$$\Sigma F_y = 0 \implies F_{4y} + Y = 0 \implies F_{4y} = -Y$$
where $X$ and $Y$ are the resultant components of the three given forces.

Resolve the three forces along the positive $x$-axis:
$$X = 18 + 12\sin 60^\circ - 8\sin 30^\circ$$
Substitute $\sin 60^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ and $\sin 30^\circ = \frac{1}{2}$:
$$X = 18 + 6\sqrt{3} - 4 = 14 + 6\sqrt{3} \approx 24.3923\text{ N}$$

Resolve the three forces along the positive $y$-axis:
$$Y = 8\cos 30^\circ + 12\cos 60^\circ$$
Substitute $\cos 30^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ and $\cos 60^\circ = \frac{1}{2}$:
$$Y = 4\sqrt{3} + 6 = 6 + 4\sqrt{3} \approx 12.9282\text{ N}$$

State the magnitude formula for the balancing force:
$$F = \sqrt{F_{4x}^2 + F_{4y}^2} = \sqrt{X^2 + Y^2}$$
Compute the sum of squares:
$$X^2 = (14 + 6\sqrt{3})^2 = 196 + 168\sqrt{3} + 108 = 304 + 168\sqrt{3} \approx 594.985$$
$$Y^2 = (6 + 4\sqrt{3})^2 = 36 + 48\sqrt{3} + 48 = 84 + 48\sqrt{3} \approx 167.138$$
$$X^2 + Y^2 = 388 + 216\sqrt{3} \approx 762.124$$
$$F = \sqrt{762.124} \approx 27.6066 \approx 27.6\text{ N}$$

Determine the direction angle $\alpha$:
$$\tan\alpha = \frac{|F_{4y}|}{|F_{4x}|} = \frac{12.9282}{24.3923} \approx 0.5300$$
$$\alpha = \tan^{-1}(0.5300) \approx 27.92^\circ \approx 27.9^\circ$$
Because $F_{4x} < 0$ and $F_{4y} < 0$, the vector points into the third quadrant, which is $27.9^\circ$ below the negative $x$-axis.

ai_rubric.Applying Coplanar Equilibrium: Resolves forces to find components $X = 14 + 6\sqrt{3}$ and $Y = 6 + 4\sqrt{3}$, computes magnitude $F = 27.6\text{ N}$, and finds direction $27.9^\circ$ below the negative $x$-axis.
ai_rubric.Resolving Forces Along Chosen Axes: Resolves all three coplanar forces along horizontal and vertical directions.
